newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police arrest 43 Shi'ite Moslems.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police arrest 43 Shi'ite Moslems.

text.p: Police in the northern state of Sokoto have arrested 43 members of a Shi'ite Moslem group allegedly planning to breach the peace in the area, the News Agency of Nigeria reported on Saturday.
Sokoto state police commissioner Gimba Umar told reporters there on Friday that the Shi'ites were picked up for inciting and making intimidating statements.
They had also been abusing the police, army and other people in authority, Umar said, adding that law-enforcement agencies in the state were battle-ready to deal with Moslem fanatics.

Two police and five Shi'ites were killed in northern Nigeria last September when supporters of the fundamentalist Shi'ite Moslem Brothers group demanding the release of their arrested leader, Sheikh Ibrahim Yakub El-Zak-Zaky, fought the police.
Police say El-Zak-Zaky, a radical preacher, was arrested because of illegal publications and radio broadcasts. He was also alleged to have imported arms. He is still in detention.
According to the Shi'ite group, 14 people were killed in clashes with police a day after El-Zak-Zaky's arrest.
The group is campaigning for the imposition of Islamic Sharia law in Africa's most populous nation, although only about half the 100 million people are Moslems, mainly of the Sunni sect.
